title: Android Backup Plan: Save Photos, WhatsApp Chats and Contacts
html:
A good Android backup plan has three layers: Google backup for your phone data, Google Photos for pictures and videos, and a separate backup for WhatsApp chats and contacts. Turn on all three, check them once a month, and keep one extra copy somewhere other than your phone. That takes about 20 minutes to set up, and it protects you if the phone is lost, stolen, dropped or simply stops working.

Last updated: 29 Oct 2026. Menu names differ between brands and Android versions; if you cannot find one, type its name into the Settings search box. The steps below follow Google's and WhatsApp's own help pages, and I have noted where a menu may look different on your phone.

Why one backup is not enough

Most people have a backup that they set up once and never looked at again. The problem is that each kind of data lives in a different place. Your contacts and settings are covered by Google backup. Your photos are covered by Google Photos. Your WhatsApp chats are covered by WhatsApp's own backup. If one of these is switched off, you only find out when you need it.

A common rule from the backup world is to keep several copies, in more than one place, with at least one away from the device. For a phone, that simply means: your data on the phone, a copy in your Google account, and a copy on a computer or drive.

Before you start: check your lock screen and storage

Two small things decide whether the rest works.

  • Use a PIN, pattern or password. Google's help page advises against a swipe or Smart Lock screen if you want your backed-up data protected.
  • Check your free space. Google gives up to 15 GB of free storage, and that space is shared by Google Photos, Google Drive and Gmail. If it is nearly full, backups will struggle, so clear some space or buy more storage first. If your phone storage is also full, read why Android storage stays full after deleting files.

Layer 1: Turn on Google backup for device data

This layer covers the things that make a new phone feel like your old one.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Google services (on some phones it is Google), then All services.
  3. Under Backup, choose what to back up: Photos & videos, Device data, or both.
  4. Turn Backup on. To run one straight away, tap Back up now.

According to Google, a device backup includes apps and app data, call history, contacts, device settings, and SMS and MMS messages. Some Google apps add more: Google Messages can back up RCS messages, and the Phone app can back up call settings and blocked numbers.

Know the limits so they do not surprise you:

  • Not every app backs up all of its settings and data.
  • A Google One backup can take up to 24 hours to show as complete.
  • You cannot restore a backup from a newer Android version onto an older one.
  • Work-profile and company-owned devices cannot use this backup.

To see what is included on your phone, go to Settings, then Google services, then Backup, and read the Backup details section.

Layer 2: Back up photos and videos with Google Photos

Photos are usually the one thing people cannot replace, so give them their own layer.

  1. Open the Google Photos app and sign in with the Google account you want to use.
  2. Tap your profile picture at the top right.
  3. Tap Photos settings, then Backup.
  4. Turn Backup on.

To check that it is working, tap your profile picture again. The status reads "Backup complete" when everything is saved, or "Backup is off" if it has been disabled. For one photo, open it, tap More, then About, and look at the Details to see whether that item is backed up.

You can change the backup quality at any time. Original quality keeps full detail but uses more of your free storage, so check which option you chose if your storage fills up quickly. If you ever delete a photo by mistake, here is how to recover deleted photos on Android.

Layer 3: WhatsApp chats and your contacts

WhatsApp chat backup

WhatsApp does not rely on the Google device backup for your chats. It has its own backup, which on Android saves to Google Drive. Open WhatsApp, go to Settings, then Chats, then Chat backup, and tap Back up. You can also choose how often it backs up automatically and whether to include videos. The wording can differ slightly between WhatsApp versions.

WhatsApp also offers an optional end-to-end encrypted backup. You protect the backup with a password you choose or with a 64-digit key that only you know, and neither WhatsApp nor the backup provider can read it. The catch is simple: if you forget the password or lose the key, you should assume the backup cannot be opened. Write it down somewhere safe before you turn the option on. WhatsApp says this feature rolled out gradually, so you may not see it on an older version.

Moving to a new phone soon? Read how to move WhatsApp chats to a new Android phone before you reset anything.

Contacts: keep a file copy too

Contacts saved to your Google account sync with Google Contacts and with your other Android devices. That is already a backup, as long as your contacts are saved to the Google account and not only to the phone or SIM. If you are not sure, open a contact, use the option to move it to another account, and pick your Google account. Remember that moving a contact removes it from the original account.

For a copy you control, export your contacts once in a while:

  1. On a computer, go to contacts.google.com and sign in.
  2. Select the contacts you want, or use Selection Actions and choose All.
  3. Click More actions at the top right, then Export.
  4. Choose Google CSV and click Export to save the file.

Add one copy outside Google

If your Google account gets locked or hacked, everything in the three layers can be out of reach at once. So once a month, copy your most important files to a computer or an external drive: the exported contacts file, and any photos or documents you cannot lose. You do not need to copy everything, only what would hurt to lose.

Protecting the account itself matters just as much, so see the Google account security checklist, and set up a way back in if your authenticator app goes missing with this recovery guide.

Check it once a month

A backup you have never checked is only a hope. Set a reminder for the first of each month and run through the list above. The whole check takes two minutes, and it is the step most people skip.

What to do next

  1. Check your screen lock and free Google storage.
  2. Turn on Google backup for device data and tap Back up now.
  3. Turn on Google Photos backup and wait for "Backup complete".
  4. Run a WhatsApp chat backup, and decide about the encrypted option.
  5. Export your contacts and copy the file to a computer.
  6. Set a monthly reminder to check all of it.

  • Back up photos and videos (Google Photos Help)
  • Export, back up or restore contacts (Google Contacts Help)
